name: NetClass Technology Inc.

profile.description: NetClass Technology is a B2B smart education IT solutions provider offering online professional education platforms, teaching management systems, and AI-powered language assessment tools across China, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Japan. The company completed a 1-for-50 share consolidation effective July 6, 2026 to attempt to regain Nasdaq minimum bid price compliance, with a compliance deadline of July 27, 2026.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): NetClass's AI Foreign Language Teaching System is now live at 71 colleges across 20 provinces in China, serving over 20,000 teachers and students across 500+ courses and generating 300,000+ contextual dialogues [2] — a modest extension of the existing education platform rather than a transformative pivot, and revenue has still declined 2.9% YoY to $9.81M. AI Deployment (2/2): The company has been pre-training and fine-tuning large AI models since 2023 and the AI Foreign Language Teaching System is commercially deployed with quantified usage across 71 institutions [2][3]. Market Share (0/2): Revenue continues to decline in a massive Chinese ed-tech market dominated by far larger players; no evidence of share gains [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Management states 2026 strategy will center on large language models applied to education and HR verticals with RAG and multi-agent technology integration, but no specific product launch dates or revenue targets were disclosed [3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No evidence of above-industry R&D spend; deepening losses (net loss widened 137% in 1H 2025 vs. 1H 2024) suggest capital constraints on sustained R&D investment [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): NetClass's stated ambition 'to become a globally leading AI technology and service provider in education and human resources' remains generic and interchangeable with peer ed-tech companies, offering no distinctive purpose [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No evidence of charitable giving or community investment programs. Employee Retention (0/2): The board comprises entirely new directors with no experienced or continuing board members, a governance red flag rather than evidence of organizational stability [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of insider open-market purchases was found; the company's imminent Nasdaq delisting risk makes insider conviction data especially relevant and its absence notable.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED: Post-reverse-split average daily volume of 67,905 shares x $4.47 stock price = ~$303,516 daily dollar volume, well below the $1M minimum threshold — Infrastructure score forced to 0 [1]. Underlying fundamentals are also deeply distressed: TTM revenue of $9.81M declined 2.9% YoY, net loss widened to -$10.82M (a 632.5% deterioration in net income), and 1H 2025 net loss of $4.90M represented a 137% widening from 1H 2024 [1][3]. The company executed a 1-for-50 share consolidation effective July 6, 2026 to avoid Nasdaq delisting, with the stock still tumbling over 25% on the announcement and now facing a hard compliance deadline of July 27, 2026 [3].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (2/9): NetClass's legacy online education courseware business is directly exposed to disruption from far larger, better-capitalized AI-native education competitors (Chinese tech giants and global platforms like Duolingo), and the company's own deepening losses (-110% profit margin, net loss widening 137% YoY in 1H 2025) show it lacks the capital to defend its position [1][3]. The AI Foreign Language Teaching System pivot is a survival response to this exact threat rather than a position of structural protection. AI Opportunity (1/1): The AI Foreign Language Teaching System is commercially live at 71 colleges serving 20,000+ users, and the company has publicly framed 2026 strategy around monetizing large language models in education and HR — a real, if still small-scale, AI product line [2][3].

infinite_game.summary: NetClass Technology is in survival mode: a reactive AI pivot amid a shrinking legacy business, a board with no experienced or continuing directors, a stock that has fallen so far it required a 1-for-50 reverse split, and a Nasdaq delisting deadline of July 27, 2026 that could end the company's public listing within days of this screen. There is no evidence of a Just Cause, courageous long-term investment, or organizational trust — every available signal points to a finite-game company fighting for its next quarter.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): The ambition to become 'a globally leading AI technology and service provider' is a competitive goal, not a Just Cause — there is no articulated vision of a better future for learners, only a desire to survive and grow market position [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The board is composed entirely of new directors with no experienced or continuing members, a structural red flag for organizational stability, compounded by a Nasdaq delisting deadline just days after this screen date that would create acute anxiety for the 46-person team [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of NetClass publicly acknowledging competitors' strengths; company messaging focuses on becoming a market leader rather than learning from larger, better-funded rivals [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The continued pivot from traditional courseware to AI-powered language assessment and LLM-based products shows genuine adaptation, but it is a necessity-driven response to a shrinking core business rather than a proactive strategic choice [2][3].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): No evidence of leadership sacrificing near-term results for long-term capability; the 1-for-50 reverse split and imminent delisting deadline reflect a company managing for near-term compliance survival rather than making bold long-term bets [3].

investment_thesis: NetClass Technology's sole remaining bull case is its AI Foreign Language Teaching System, now deployed at 71 colleges across 20 provinces in China with 20,000+ teachers and students and 500+ courses, alongside a stated 2026 strategy to apply large language models, RAG, and multi-agent technology across education and HR verticals [2][3]. The company has been developing proprietary large AI models since 2023, providing some technical credibility to the AI pivot. Revenue of $9.81M, while declining, still represents an existing customer base of Chinese universities that could theoretically be upsold on AI products.
thesis_continued: The bear case is now acute and time-bound. NetClass completed a 1-for-50 reverse share split effective July 6, 2026 specifically to avoid Nasdaq delisting, and faces a hard compliance deadline of July 27, 2026 — just nine days after this screen date — with the stock still trading in penny-stock territory post-split [3]. Net loss widened to -$10.82M (a 632.5% deterioration), and 1H 2025 losses widened 137% YoY, indicating the AI pivot has not yet stemmed the financial bleeding [3]. Post-split average daily dollar volume of roughly $303,516 sits far below the IOWN $1M liquidity floor, triggering an automatic Infrastructure score of 0. A board composed entirely of new, inexperienced directors adds governance risk on top of the existential financial and listing risk [3].
key_catalysts: Successful Nasdaq compliance by the July 27, 2026 deadline, removing the immediate delisting overhang that is suppressing investor interest
Scaling of the AI Foreign Language Teaching System beyond the current 71 colleges and 20,000 users into a revenue base large enough to offset legacy courseware decline
A strategic acquirer or investor stepping in given the company's proprietary large-AI-model development since 2023, ahead of a potential delisting
key_risks: Imminent Nasdaq delisting risk — compliance deadline of July 27, 2026 is just days away from this screen date, with failure resulting in loss of public listing and severe liquidity destruction for remaining shareholders
Deepening losses — net loss widened 632.5% to -$10.82M with 1H 2025 losses widening 137% YoY, showing the AI pivot has not yet reversed the financial trajectory

Sub-$1M daily liquidity (~$303,516) makes the stock effectively untradeable at institutional scale and triggers the IOWN hard liquidity floor, forcing Infrastructure to zero regardless of any operational improvement
